newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Monday with most investors staying on the sidelines, traders said.

The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended at 3,347 yuan ($403) per tonne, surging 216 yuan due to speculation, traders said. It opened at 3,347 yuan per tonne and stayed at that level for the whole session.
Other contracts moved narrowly. September fell one yuan to 3,209, November dropped nine yuan to 3,211, the January 1998 contract lost two to 3,158 and March rose 12 to 3,140 yuan.
Combined volume fell to 19,000 tonnes from 36,200 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved around the opening level for most of the session, traders said.
"A lack of market moving news kept most investors on the sidelines today," one trader said.
"The active domestic stock markets also attracted the attention of many retail investors," he added.
Traders said they expected most soybean contracts to continue to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
